subject: Clarify per-tenant log retention & legal-hold path for Meridian Health
messages:
From: Jane Fletcher <jane.fletcher@meridian-health.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Meridian Security <security@meridian-health.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T08:03:00-08:00
Subject: Questions on per-tenant log retention & legal hold

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for taking this. Meridian's security and legal teams have a few narrow but urgent questions as we evaluate Redwood for production use in our patient-facing services:

- What are the default retention windows for: request logs (full request/response payload), access/auth logs, and system-level debug traces for hosted customers?
- Can Redwood place a "legal hold" on a single tenant's logs (not account-wide) to prevent deletion beyond the normal TTL? If so, what is the process and what proof/signatures do you require?
- Is selective PII redaction or tokenization supported before long-term storage (we'd prefer not to retain raw PHI if avoidable)?
- For SOC 2 / SIG evidence: can you provide mapping or an attestation that legal-hold events are captured in audit logs and that retention overrides are visible in your Console?

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our questions and a sample incident timeline. We need this to feed into our procurement and privacy review this month.

Thanks,
Jane Fletcher\Principal Security Engineer\Meridian Health

Attachment: Meridian-SIG-questions.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Fletcher <jane.fletcher@meridian-health.com>
Cc: Meridian Security <security@meridian-health.com>
Date: 2026-11-12T12:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on per-tenant log retention & legal hold

Hi Jane —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below and I attached our retention matrix for quick reference. I'll loop in our compliance and product ops to confirm any customer-specific work.

Summary (short):
- Default (hosted): request payloads (full) = 90 days; access/auth logs = 180 days; aggregated telemetry/metrics = 13 months.
- Legal hold for a tenant: yes — we can implement a per-tenant retention override that prevents automated deletion for an agreed period. This requires a signed legal-hold request from the customer + approval from Redwood compliance.
- Redaction/tokenization: we support a selective masking pipeline (PII redaction) as an add-on. For PHI, we recommend redaction at ingest + storing tokenized payloads if you want to avoid retaining raw identifiers.
- Evidence/SOC 2: holds and retention overrides generate Console audit events (audit.log) and we can provide an export for SIG/SOC 2 reviewers. We will provide an attestation + a sample audit export.

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick call (30m) this week so we can confirm the exact scope (duration, which log classes to hold, masking vs raw retention).
2) If Meridian wants a proof-of-concept (POC), we can enable a 30-day tenant hold in a test cluster and produce an audit trace.
3) If you need extended retention (6-24 months) we can propose either: Dedicated pool or a Private deployment, or a hosted override with explicit billing adjustments and an executed legal-hold addendum.

Attachment: redwood_log_retention_matrix_v2.pdf (PDF)

Happy to schedule the call — what times work for you?

— Sergio
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T09:10:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions on per-tenant log retention & legal hold

Neha/Kim — forwarding Meridian's request and my initial answers. They asked if we can do a tenant-specific legal hold for an incident that may involve PHI. A few implementation notes / ask:

- We should be able to flip a retention_override flag per tenant; that would mark objects with a retention_control tag and exempt them from ordinary TTL deletion.
- For PHI cases I want to avoid retaining raw payloads long-term. Can we offer: ingest-time PII redaction (PII -> tokens) + retain tokenized payloads for X months, while retaining full encrypted raw payloads only for a short incident window (e.g., 90 days)?
- Need compliance sign-off for: (a) where we store held data (S3 bucket vs GCP object store), (b) whether we can support WORM (write-once) for that bucket, and (c) whether we can surface the hold/unhold events in audit logs for SIG evidence.

I'm attaching a short legal hold request template that we can send to Meridian for signatures. Also need a quick estimate of storage delta and cost for a 2-year hold on 100 GB of logs.

Attachment: legal_hold_request_template.docx (DOCX)

Thoughts?
— Sergio

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-13T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on per-tenant log retention & legal hold

Sergio —

Quick answers from compliance/product side:
- Per-tenant retention override is feasible. Implementation approach we prefer: dedicated retention policy object attached to tenant metadata (retention_policy_id). This is surfaced in the Console and emitted to audit.log whenever applied/removed.
- For PHI: recommend redaction at ingest and encrypted raw payloads moved to a restricted bucket with separate KMS key and access control. For WORM-style protections we can leverage object-store retention policies (if customer provides an S3 bucket/backed integration) or emulate via immutability flags and strict RBAC for our hosted offering.
- Cost: rough ballpark for 100 GB retained for 2 years on standard storage + encryption + additional access logs is ~$1,800–$2,500 depending on egress needs and retrieval frequency. We should produce a formal quote for Meridian's exact volumes.

One compliance caveat: our SOC 2 attestation covers that retention overrides are logged and that we have change control around retention policy objects, but extended retention that stores PHI for multiple years may require an MSA amendment and privacy review. Kimberly, can you prepare an MSA amendment draft (short clause) that covers: retention override authorization, billing impact, and proof-of-hold evidence?

— Neha

From: Jane Fletcher <jane.fletcher@meridian-health.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Meridian Security <security@meridian-health.com>, Meridian Legal <legal-ops@meridian-health.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Questions on per-tenant log retention & legal hold

Sergio —

Thanks for the quick clarifications and Neha — thanks for the cost ballpark. Meridian is comfortable proceeding with a conservative POC:

Scope: enable a 30-day tenant-level hold in a sandbox/test tenant, apply ingest-time PII redaction for request payloads, and produce the audit export showing hold events and access logs.
Acceptance criteria: we can see the retention_override tag in the audit export and confirm payloads are tokenized in stored copies.
Timeline: we'd like a 2-week timeline for POC enablement if feasible.

Please send the legal-hold form and a short statement of work + cost. If the POC results are satisfactory, we'll discuss extended retention options and MSA amendment.

Jane Fletcher\Principal Security Engineer\Meridian Health

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

3) Neha/QE will validate that payloads are tokenized in the stored copy per the POC (target validation window: 48 hours after hold is engaged).
4) Kimberly will draft an MSA amendment for extended retention billing and privacy language if you decide to move beyond POC.

I've attached a preliminary cost-estimate for the POC and a link to the Jira ticket that will track work. Please confirm the contact for legal hold sign-off (name/email) so we can send the form.
